gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'I can swim,' the boy boasted. The boy boasted that he ___ swim.
gaps.explanation: Can backshifts to could in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'Thank you for delivering it so quickly,' she said. She ___ me for delivering it so quickly.
gaps.explanation: Thanks are reported as thank somebody for + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.
